## Summary

Adds a warning when neither `--num_requests` nor `--duration` is specified. The warning states that the full dataset will run and recommends setting an explicit limit.

## Dev Engineer Review

- The warning applies only when both benchmark limits are unset.
- The change does not alter public APIs or benchmark behavior.
- Python syntax validation passed.
- No configuration or test-list files changed.

## Description

<!--
Added a warning in the TensorRT-LLM latency benchmark when no runtime limit is specified.

Previously, users could launch a latency benchmark without setting either:
- `--num_requests`
- `--duration`

For large datasets, this could unintentionally result in long-running benchmark jobs and unnecessary GPU resource usage.

This change adds a warning after benchmark configuration parsing to inform users that the full dataset will be processed and recommends setting an explicit benchmark limit.
-->

Generated by an AI-assisted triage bot; please correct any mistaken assumptions.

The warning gives users a timely reminder that an uncapped run will process the dataset. As implemented, it leaves execution unchanged, so its demonstrated benefit is limited to that notice.

Based on the assessment above, we're giving this PR lower review priority for now and adding `waiting for feedback` and `stale`.

Evidence that the warning prevents a practical resource-use problem beyond informing users of the existing limit options would warrant reconsideration.
